A: Explanation and story behind What Log4j 2 use internally is what they call a ShutdownRegistrationStrategy. It consist of a class that register one or many shutdown callback(s) that would be called at the appropriate time. texts.full_text: uslim men stormed the police station where he was held, attacked and injured police officers on the scene, and seized the hapless Abbas. As reported earlier by Spero, as well as other news agencies, the mob beat Abbas on the street and doused him with gasoline, setting him alight. A police officer on the scene averred that Abbas was still alive when he became a human torch, unlike reports made of the incident by Al Jazeera. Pakistan non-governmental organizations, Christian groups, and others have denounced the outrage. Pakistani President Aisf Ali Zardari has expressed regret over this most recent instance in his country where religious fanaticism leads to violence against innocents who are deemed blasphemers under Islamic law or Shariah. The president called for justice on July 9 after Abbas was burned alive. “Such heinous acts of intolerance and extremism have no place among us. Those responsible must be held accountable,” said Zardari, according to the BBC News Service (UK). Zia-ud-Din Tabbaei is a Pakistani political scientist who has written extensively on Islamic fundamentalism in Pakistan for various publications. He told Spero that it was too early to say whether Abbas had been mentally ill or not. But he said there were many other factors involved with the incident, such as “the local government’s failure” and lack of police protection. “The blasphemy law has become a weapon against minorities,” Tabbaei added. In 2011, Pakistan ranked fourth among countries in which religious freedom was denied by Open Doors USA. The group cited persecution from Islamic fundamentalists for that denial (see: http://www.speroforum.com/a/OO4KX9YI7D8/religious-freedom-in-10-countries-open-doors-usa-report). texts.full_text: with whom he won the European Cup. Club career Wrexham Jones joined Wrexham in 1971. He made his debut at the age of 17 in a Welsh Cup tie against local rivals Chester City; Wrexham lost 1–0. He did, however, win the Welsh Cup with the club in 1975, when they beat Cardiff City in the final. Jones established himself as a right-back and helped Wrexham to the quarter-finals of the FA Cup in 1974, the first time the club had reached that stage. Liverpool Jones left Wfor Liverpool on transfer deadline day at Christmas during his second season with them (a few days after he turned eighteen). He was immediately handed a place by manager Bob Paisley and made an impressive debut in February 1974 against Leeds United, which ended as one of the most memorable matches between these two sides. Jones played every minute for Liverpool that year. Jones quickly established himself at Anfield under both managers: first with Bill Shankly until his retirement after winning a league title (he was on crutches when he handed over to Paisley), and then Bob's successor, who took him all the way in European competition during an illustrious period. Jones won five First Division titles as well two League Cups. His best season came under Joe Fagan’s management: Liverpool finished top of both league tables (the first time this had been achieved) with 68 points from a possible total and he scored four goals, including one against Arsenal in the FA Cup semi-final replay. The Reds also won their sixth European title at Wembley Stadium by beating Club Brugge; Jones was an ever-present that season. Injuries plagued him towards his time out of Liverpool: first with Croxteth Park's own Bob Paisley and then under Fagan, but he made a successful return to the team in 1981. texts.full_text: chain slowly beginning to catch up to strong demand for the popular device… A quick glance over the iPhone 5 listing on the US online Apple store reveals a 2-3 week delivery estimate for new orders, down from the previously quoted 3-4 weeks estimate. It’s welcome news to folks who’ve been on the lookout for Apple’s new phone. It remains to be seen when Apple will reach the supply-demand balance. Apple CEO Tim Cook told analysts on a conference call last month that “the demand for iPhone 5 is extremely robust”, adding that Apple is “in a significant state of backlog”. If history is an indication, it’s gonna be awhile before we see estimated iPhone 5 shipping times dropping from weeks to days. The iPhone 4S shipping times had been sitting at 1-2 weeks for nearly three months before inventory levels improved. Let’s not forget that Apple has yet to release the iPhone 5 in China and a number of other markets worldwide. The aggressive roll-out should see the company launching the device in over a hundred countries and across 240 carriers by year’s end. What’s important, I think, is that Apple is finally making progress toward meeting demand for the handset,

texts.full_text: dvice for dating from bestselling dating book and romantic comedy author Lisa Daily BEDIQUETTE: What your sleeping habits say about your relationship. February 28, 2015 Snuggle all night or separate beds? This week on Daytime I’m talking about what your sleeping habits say about your relationship. Turns out, a recent study from Ryerson University in Toronto found that 30 – 40% of couples don’t sleep in the same bed, which is what we’ll be talking about this week on the Daytime show. Is sleeping separately a sign of relationship doom? Oddly enough, the answer is no. Some couples just need their own space. Maybe your partner snores or has medical issues, or tosses and turns all night. Lots of couples sleep separately, and it doesn’t mean that their relationship is doomed. That said, if you went from snuggling all night to separate sides of the bed to separate bedrooms, you may be experiencing some trouble in your relationship.
